register_pressure.risk: Need careful per-thread accumulator count; hidden=128 channels in MLP.

nodes.notes:
1) CLASSIFICATION: Fused Swin transformer block (LN+W-MSA+residual+LN+MLP+residual). Window size 4x4=16 tokens, single head, dim=32, hidden=128. Image 720x1280 -> 180x320=57600 windows. Each window is fully independent. Mixed: reductions (LN, softmax), small matmuls, elementwise+GELU. Dense access. Small&fixed: N=16, C=32, H_mlp=128, num_heads=1. Large: number of windows (57600).
2) MATH: Per window of 16 tokens x 32 ch: y1=LN(x); qkv=y1@Wqkv+b -> Q,K,V (16x32 each); attn=softmax(Q@K^T/sqrt(32)+rpe); o=attn@V; p=o@Wproj+b; r1=x+p; y2=LN(r1); h=GELU(r1@W1+b1) (16x128); out=r1+h@W2+b2. All weights tiny, fully reusable across windows.
3) LAYOUT: Input (1,720,1280,32) row-major; window partition rearranges to (Bw=57600,16,32). Each window reads 16*32=512 fp16 contiguous-ish (but strided: 16 rows of 4 contig tokens, 4 such row-groups). Weights: load once into groupshared (read-only tile) shared by all threads.
4) REGIMES: (a) bandwidth-bound streaming if fused — limit ~0.13ms; (b) compute-bound if matmuls dominate (negligible: ~few MFLOP per window × 57600 ~= modest); (c) sync/divergence-bound if too many barriers per window. Bottleneck likely memory bandwidth.
5) KNOBS: window-per-wave vs window-per-block; cache weights in groupshared vs registers; vectorize loads as half4; softmax via wave intrinsics; layout of token-per-lane (16 lanes used) vs 2-tokens-per-lane.
6) SKELETON: One wave (32 lanes) owns one window. Lanes 0..15 = tokens, lanes 16..31 idle OR each lane handles 2 channel-halves. Better: 16 lanes own one token each; the 32-ch vector held per-lane in registers (half2x8 or 8 halves). LN reduce via WaveActiveSum across lanes 0..15 (masked). qkv@W via per-lane MAC over channels broadcasting weight from groupshared. Attn: each lane has Q,K,V row; compute QK^T via WaveReadLaneAt to fetch K rows; softmax via wave max/sum on 16-element vector held per lane. MLP hidden=128 done in chunks of 32 via 4 register tiles per lane. All weights in groupshared (shared across the threadgroup), loaded once.
7) FAMILIES: (A) One-wave-per-window full fusion [PREFERRED, top]: 1 threadgroup = 1 or few waves, each wave one window; weights cached in groupshared once per group; activations register-resident; minimal barriers (only at weight-load + a few softmax-broadcast points using wave intrinsics not barriers). (B) Multi-wave-per-window collaborative: split MLP hidden across waves; needs groupshared exchange — extra barriers, not worth it given window is small. (C) Multi-pass kernels (LN/QKV/attn/MLP separate dispatches): NOT allowed (single-dispatch runner) and would be bandwidth-disastrous.
FULL FUSION: working set per wave is 16 tokens × 32 ch fp16 = 1KB register-distributed (32B/lane = 16 halves/lane); weights ~13K fp16 in groupshared (26KB ≤ 32KB cap). Highly feasible.

action.description: Implement one threadgroup = multiple waves, each wave owns one independent 4x4 window. 32 lanes per wave: lanes 0..15 hold one token's 32-channel vector in registers (as 16 halves per lane via half2 arrays); lanes 16..31 mirror/help with MLP hidden=128. Load all weight tensors (qkv,proj,fc1,fc2,norms,rpe ~26KB) into groupshared once per threadgroup. Execute LN1, QKV proj, scaled QK^T with rpe, softmax (wave reductions across 16 active lanes), AV, proj, residual, LN2, FC1, GELU, FC2, residual, store. Use WaveReadLaneAt to broadcast peer-token K/V rows. Single dispatch covers all 57600 windows.
action.rationale: Avoids all intermediate global traffic; reduces to ~118MB streamed I/O ≈ 0.13ms lower bound. Reference fp16 PyTorch likely 2-5ms.
action.title: Full-fusion one-wave-per-window with groupshared weight tile

kernel_summary: Fused Swin transformer block over (1,720,1280,32) fp16: per non-overlapping 4x4 window (16 tokens, dim=32, single head, MLP hidden=128) compute LN1 -> QKV linear -> scaled dot-product attention with 16x16 relative position bias -> softmax -> AV -> proj -> add residual -> LN2 -> FC1 -> GELU -> FC2 -> add residual. 57600 independent windows. All weights are tiny (~26KB fp16 total) and reusable across windows; activations per window are 1KB. Likely bandwidth-bound on 118MB I/O (~0.13ms floor at 896GB/s); the key win is full fusion in a single dispatch so no intermediate tensor hits global memory. cs_6_8 with 32KB groupshared cap and no MMA intrinsics; rely on wave intrinsics (size 32) for softmax/LN reductions and broadcasts. Map one wave (or two windows per wave) to one window, with weights loaded once into groupshared per threadgroup.
open_questions: Exact PyTorch fp16 reference latency on RTX5090 Mobile to size speedup targets.
Are window loads better issued as half4 vectors or scalar halves given the 4-element-contiguous-per-row stride pattern?
Does cs_6_8 support float16_t arithmetic intrinsics (exp, rsqrt) with sufficient throughput, or should softmax/LN use fp32 accumulators?
How many threadgroups should we launch per dispatch (one per window vs multiple windows per threadgroup) to maximize SM occupancy while amortizing the weight load?
Will the MLP hidden=128 chunked computation cause register spills if held per-lane, and is streaming through fc1->GELU->fc2 channel-by-channel cheaper?
Optimal lane-to-data mapping for the 16x16 attention matrix: token-per-lane with WaveReadLaneAt for K rows, or pair-of-tokens-per-lane?
Numerical stability of softmax in fp16 with rpe added — need fp32 max/sum reduction?
Does the runner accept [WaveSize(32)] attribute under cs_6_8, and is wave broadcast latency low enough to outperform groupshared scratch?
